nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
2/ What is hMPV?
hMPV is a viral respiratory infection from the Paramyxoviridae family. It causes symptoms ranging from mild colds to severe pneumonia, particularly in children, the elderly, and those with weak immune systems.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
3/ Symptoms to Watch For:

Runny nose

Cough

Fever

Difficulty breathing

Wheezing
If you or someone close to you has these symptoms, take them seriously.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
4/ How Does It Spread?
hMPV spreads through:

Respiratory droplets (sneezing/coughing)

Touching contaminated surfaces

Close contact with infected individuals

Good hygiene is your first defense.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
5/ Diagnosis:
Doctors use PCR tests, viral cultures, or serology to confirm hMPV. Consult general physicians, pulmonologists, or pediatricians for proper evaluation if symptoms worsen.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
6/ Treatment:
There’s no specific antiviral yet. Treatment focuses on symptom management:

Rest

Hydration

Fever reducers

Oxygen therapy for severe cases

Early intervention can save lives.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
7/ Precautions:

Wash hands frequently

Wear masks in crowded areas

Avoid close contact with sick individuals

Disinfect commonly touched surfaces

These small steps can help curb the spread

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
nodes.text:
8/ 🌍 Why the Global Concern?
The rapid spread of hMPV is alarming. Experts warn that global travel and dense urban settings could accelerate its transmission. Stay informed and vigilant.

nodes.author: Jagajjiban_m
